I am 49 years old and have farmed these 60 mu in Quzhou for 25 years. I know this land, and I know where every yuan goes. With four in the household but some of us working off-farm for part of the year, I am short on labor. I cannot chase every new input the shopkeepers push. I stick to what pays back.

I will keep 50 mu in my wheat-maize double crop. That is my foundation — it is mechanized, predictable, and the buyers are always there. The other 10 mu I will plant to cotton. Cotton is more work and more sprays, but the price per mu can beat maize when the market is right, and I have enough experience with it to keep the losses low.

For the winter wheat already in the ground from last autumn: I sowed an improved variety that has done well here for years — not the newest, expensive seed, but reliable. I will topdress with about 15 kg of nitrogen per mu, plus some phosphorus and potassium at green-up. Three irrigations from my well: one at regreening if the winter was dry, one at jointing, and one at heading. More than that, and the electricity bill eats the profit. I will spray herbicide once in early spring, and two more times for aphids and powdery mildew if they show up. I expect around 450 kg per mu if the spring weather holds.

For summer maize: As soon as the wheat comes off in early June, I will plant hybrid maize directly into the stubble with no tillage. There is no time to waste before the summer heat hits, and skipping tillage saves diesel and labor. I will put compound fertilizer down at sowing and side-dress at the big-flush stage for about 16 kg nitrogen per mu. Two irrigations: one when the plants are knee-high and one during grain filling. Three sprays in total — one pre-emergence herbicide and two for corn borers and leaf blight. With a normal summer, 550 kg per mu is what I aim for.

For cotton on the 10 mu: I will plough that land deep in spring because cotton roots need loose soil down deep. I will plant a hybrid Bt cotton variety. It needs more fertility than the grain crops — about 18 kg nitrogen per mu, split between basal and flowering. Three irrigations: at flowering, boll setting, and boll opening. The bollworms are less trouble now with Bt seed, but the aphids and mites still come, so I will spray ten times through the season — herbicide early, then insecticide and growth regulators when I see the need. I expect about 250 kg of seed cotton per mu.

I keep my inputs moderate. I have watched young neighbors pour fertilizer and water onto their fields and end up with lodged wheat or empty profit. After 25 years, I know the point where spending more stops earning more.
